mainTopic: Who brings which פסח when the community is half טהור and half טמא: רב vs. two versions of רב כהנא, tested against the משנה and three ברייתות
overview: This amud deals with a community that is exactly half טהור and half טמא at פסח time. רב holds that each half brings its own first פסח, the טמאים בטומאה. רב כהנא has two versions: in one the טמאים go to פסח שני, and in the other they bring no פסח at all. The גמרא tests both views against the רישא and סיפא of the משנה, and each side reads the words 'רובו' and 'מיעוט' to fit its view. Next, the גמרא brings three ברייתות, one for each position. It then shows how each opinion explains away the ברייתות that disagree with it, mostly by asking whether women are counted for the first פסח and for פסח שני. For the remaining ברייתא, רב כהנא answers that תנאים argue whether half counts like a majority. Finally, the גמרא studies that ברייתא directly: if the טמאים outnumber the טהורים by even one, everyone brings the פסח בטומאה, because a קרבן ציבור is not divided. רבי אלעזר בן מתיא disagrees, and his verse comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The other opinion: impure half brings no Pesach at all
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that disagrees with רב holds that in a half-and-half case, the טמאים bring neither the first פסח nor פסח שני, and the גמרא explains why.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the impure people do not bring the קרבן פסח on the first פסח or on the second. They don't bring it on the first because they are not a majority. They don't bring it on the second because they are not a minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating the later version (לישנא בתרא) of רב כהנא's opinion, which argues with רב about a community split exactly half טהור and half טמא. It then gives the reason why the impure half loses out completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rules in the background. Only a רוב that is טמא may bring the פסח בטומאה on the first פסח. Only a מיעוט that is טמא is pushed off to פסח שני. An exact half fits neither rule, so according to this view the impure half falls through the cracks and brings nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: the first פסח, on the 14th of ניסן
פסח שני, the make-up פסח on the 14th of אייר

steps.confusionAlert: This line is NOT רב's opinion. It is the end of the opinion that argues with him. רב's view, which the rest of this passage defends, is that each half brings its own פסח on the first פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the two rules, רוב goes בטומאה and מיעוט goes to שני. The rest of the sugya reads the משנה's wording through these two rules.

phrases.english: And the impure do not perform (the Pesach)
phrases.notes: Continuing the opinion that disagrees with רב, stated on the previous amud.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: neither the first nor the second.
On the first they do not perform it —
because they are not a majority.
phrases.notes: Only an impure majority may bring the פסח בטומאה.

phrases.english: On the second they do not perform it —
because they are not a minority.
phrases.notes: Only an impure minority is deferred to פסח שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּטְמֵאִין אֵין עוֹשִׂין לֹא אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the later version of רב כהנא's view in the מחלוקת with רב about מחצה על מחצה, begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a half-and-half case, the טמאים bring neither the first פסח nor פסח שני. They are neither a רוב nor a מיעוט.

steps.title: The משנה's first clause seems to contradict רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the רישא of the משנה. It infers that only a טמא majority brings the פסח בטומאה, which implies half-and-half does not bring the first פסח. This contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If the whole community or most of it became impure, or if the כהנים were impure and the community was pure, the פסח is brought in impurity. This implies that only when most are impure do they bring it in impurity. But if it is half and half, they do not bring it on the first פסח. This is a difficulty for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב using a precise reading (דיוק) of the משנה. The משנה says 'רובו', most of the community, so exactly half seems excluded from bringing the first פסח בטומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that in a half-and-half case, everyone, including the טמאים, brings the first פסח. But the משנה only lists כל הקהל or רובו as bringing it בטומאה. By saying 'רובו', the משנה seems to teach that an exact half does not bring the first פסח, which goes against רב.

phrases.english: We learned: If the community or most of it became impure,
or if the kohanim were impure
and the community was pure —
it is performed in impurity.
It is only a majority that performs it in impurity,
phrases.notes: The גמרא's דיוק from the word 'רובו'.

phrases.english: but half and half
do not perform it on the first.
This is a difficulty for Rav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both opinions are stated, the גמרא tests רב's opinion against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that in a half-and-half case, each group brings the first פסח (the טמאים as well).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה limits bringing the פסח בטומאה to 'רובו', a majority. By implication, an exact half may not bring the first פסח בטומאה, which contradicts רב.

steps.title: רב reinterprets the משנה's first clause
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the משנה's 'רובו' means that with a טמא majority, everyone, even the טהורים, brings the פסח בטומאה. With half-and-half, each group brings its own פסח separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can answer you: When there is a majority, all of them bring it in impurity. When it is half and half, these bring their own and those bring their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the קשיא by reading the משנה's דיוק in a different way. Half-and-half is excluded only from 'everyone together בטומאה', not from the first פסח altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא assumed that 'רובו' excludes half-and-half from the first פסח. רב says the משנה's real point is that a טמא majority lets the entire community, even the pure people, bring the פסח בטומאה. Half-and-half loses only that group allowance. Each half still brings the first פסח on its own, the טהורים בטהרה and the טמאים בטומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: he could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is NOT saying half-and-half is pushed to פסח שני. Both halves still bring the first פסח. They just do it as two separate groups instead of everyone together בטומאה.

phrases.english: Rav can say to you:
With a majority, all of them perform it in impurity,
phrases.notes: Even the pure people need not guard their purity.

phrases.english: half and half —
these perform for themselves
phrases.notes: The טהורים, in purity.

phrases.english: and those perform for themselves.
phrases.notes: The טמאים, in impurity, on the first פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by narrowing what the משנה's דיוק excludes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the דיוק: what 'רובו' excludes is everyone together בטומאה, not the first פסח itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'רובו' implies that an exact half cannot bring the first פסח בטומאה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רובו' means a טמא majority lets everyone bring it בטומאה. Half-and-half still brings the first פסח, with each group separate.

steps.title: The משנה's later clause supports רב's reading
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says only a טמא minority is pushed to פסח שני, so half-and-half brings the first פסח. Since the רישא excluded half-and-half from 'all together בטומאה', it must be that each group brings its own, just as רב says.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is logical, because the latter clause teaches: If a minority of the community became impure, the pure ones bring the first פסח and the impure ones bring the second. This implies that only a minority brings it on the second, but not half and half. So they bring it on the first, and these bring their own and those bring their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב from a דיוק in the סיפא of the same משנה. Read together with the רישא, the only way to fit both clauses is רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא says 'מיעוט' goes to פסח שני, which implies that an exact half is not pushed to שני and therefore brings the first פסח. Yet the רישא implied that half-and-half does not bring it all together בטומאה. Putting both דיוקים together, half-and-half brings the first פסח with each group on its own. This is exactly רב's position.

keyTerms.meaning: so too it is logical (introduces support)
the latter clause of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In a half-and-half case, רב holds that the טהורים and the טמאים each bring the first פסח separately. The רישא (רוב goes all together בטומאה) and the סיפא (only מיעוט goes to שני) of the משנה fit together only according to רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the classic technique of combining a דיוק from the רישא with a דיוק from the סיפא. The middle case, which the משנה never states openly, gets defined this way.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
since the latter clause teaches:
If a minority of the community became impure,
the pure perform the first
and the impure perform the second.
It is only a minority that performs it on the second,
but half and half — not.
Rather, they perform it on the first,
and these perform for themselves
and those perform for themselves.
phrases.notes: Since the רישא excluded 'all together בטומאה', the groups must be separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רב's answer in step 3 with an independent דיוק from the סיפא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's reading that half-and-half brings the first פסח, with each group separate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: 'נטמא מיעוט הקהל... טמאין עושין את השני'. Only a minority is deferred, so half-and-half is not deferred.

steps.title: Now the משנה seems to be a problem for רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: After reading the משנה in favor of רב, the גמרא points out that this same reading seems to contradict רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, this is a difficulty for רב כהנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side. If the משנה supports רב, then it seems to go against רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, the סיפא was read to mean that in a half-and-half case the טמאים are not pushed off to פסח שני. That suggests they bring the first פסח. But רב כהנא (in his later version) says that in a half-and-half case the טמאים do not bring the first פסח, so the reading seems to clash with him.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who disagrees with רב about the half-and-half case
'But then' — introduces the downside of what was just said

phrases.english: But then, it is a difficulty for Rav Kahana!
phrases.notes: This builds on the reading of the סיפא from step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reading of the סיפא that supported רב and turns it against רב כהנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's view (in both versions) that in a half-and-half case the טמאים do not bring the first פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא implies that only a minority of טמאים is pushed to פסח שני. So in a half-and-half case the טמאים are not pushed off, and they seem to bring the first פסח. That goes against רב כהנא.

steps.title: רב כהנא reads the סיפא differently
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the סיפא's implication is about פסח שני: only a minority of טמאים brings פסח שני. So in a half-and-half case the טמאים do not bring פסח שני, and the רישא already showed they do not bring the first one either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא could say to you: The סיפא says that if a minority of the community became טמא, the טהורים bring the first פסח and the טמאים bring פסח שני. This implies that in a half-and-half case, the טהורים bring the first פסח, but the טמאים bring neither the first nor the second.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge. He shows that the סיפא can be read in a way that fits his view exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The precise point of the סיפא is not 'only a minority is pushed off.' Instead, it is 'only when they are a minority do the טמאים get פסח שני.' So half-and-half טמאים get no פסח שני. The רישא already said that half-and-half טמאים do not bring the first פסח בטומאה. Put the two readings together, and the טמאים bring nothing at all, which is exactly רב כהנא's later version.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This implies' — introduces a precise reading drawn from the wording
'He could say to you' — a defense given on someone's behalf

steps.confusionAlert: Both רב and רב כהנא are reading the very same words of the סיפא. They simply disagree about what the word 'minority' is meant to exclude. רב says it excludes being pushed off to פסח שני. רב כהנא says it excludes the right to bring פסח שני.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana could say to you:
If a minority of the community became impure —
phrases.notes: Quoting the סיפא of the משנה.

phrases.english: the pure ones perform the first [Pesach]
and the impure ones perform the second.
This implies that if it is half and half —
the pure ones perform the first,
but the impure ones do not perform

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: neither the first nor the second.
phrases.notes: 'Not the first' comes from the רישא. 'Not the second' comes from this reading of the סיפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate inference from the same wording (the excluded case is redefined)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'minority' implies that half-and-half טמאים are not pushed to פסח שני, so they bring the first פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'minority' implies that half-and-half טמאים do not get פסח שני. Together with the רישא, they bring neither פסח.

steps.title: But what about רב כהנא's first version?
steps.stepSummary: The answer in step 6 only works for רב כהנא's later version. In his first version, the half-and-half טמאים do bring פסח שני, so the סיפא's word 'minority' seems to contradict him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works well for the later version of רב כהנא. But according to the other version, in which רב כהנא said that the טהורים bring the first פסח and the טמאים bring פסח שני, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that רב כהנא's view was reported in two versions. It asks how the משנה fits the version that step 6 did not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, half-and-half טמאים bring פסח שני. But the סיפא says 'a minority' brings פסח שני, which implies that half-and-half טמאים do not. The defense in step 6 relied on exactly that implication, so it cannot help this version.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That works out fine' — introduces a 'but what about...' challenge
The later (second) version of a statement
'What is there to say?' — a demand for an answer

phrases.english: This works out well according to the latter version of Rav Kahana.
But according to that [other] version
in which Rav Kahana said:
the pure ones perform the first,
and the impure ones perform the second,
phrases.notes: This refers to the half-and-half case.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 6 to one version and challenges the other.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's first version: in a half-and-half case, the טמאים bring פסח שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא gives פסח שני only to a minority of טמאים. That implies half-and-half טמאים do not get פסח שני, which contradicts this version.

steps.title: 'Minority' is just a style match for 'majority'
steps.stepSummary: In the first version, half-and-half also gets פסח שני. The משנה said 'minority' only to match the wording 'majority' in the רישא, not to exclude the half-and-half case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא could say to you: The same rule applies even in a half-and-half case. The טהורים bring the first פסח, and the טמאים bring פסח שני. The reason the משנה says 'a minority of the community' is that it said 'its majority' in the רישא, so it also said 'its minority' in the סיפא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends his first version. He says the word 'minority' is not meant to exclude the half-and-half case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an exact word in a משנה is read as excluding other cases. Here the word is explained as simple parallel phrasing (רישא 'majority' and סיפא 'minority'). So no conclusion about the half-and-half case may be drawn from it, and half-and-half follows the minority rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The same law applies' — extends a rule to another case
'Since it taught' — this word was chosen only to match a parallel phrase

steps.confusionAlert: The answer 'אַיְּידֵי' means the word 'minority' teaches nothing extra. You cannot draw a precise inference from it, because the משנה chose it only for matching style.
steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא has two versions. In the later version, the סיפא's 'minority' excludes half-and-half from פסח שני, so those טמאים bring nothing. In the first version, 'minority' is just style ('אַיְּידֵי'), so half-and-half טמאים bring פסח שני.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ פַּלְגָא וּפַלְגָא נָמֵי —
phrases.english: The same law applies even to half and half as well —
the pure ones perform the first,
and the impure ones perform the second.
And the reason it teaches 'a minority of the community'
is that since it taught 'its majority' in the first clause —
it also taught 'its minority' in the latter clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב כָּהֲנָא: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ פַּלְגָא וּפַלְגָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'minority' excludes the half-and-half case from פסח שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'minority' only matches 'majority' in the רישא. Half-and-half טמאים also bring פסח שני.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there are ברייתות supporting רב and both versions of רב כהנא. It begins with one that supports רב: in a half-and-half case, each group brings its own פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with רב, and a ברייתא was taught in agreement with רב כהנא, in both of his versions. Here is the one in agreement with רב: If the Jewish people were half טהורים and half טמאים, these bring their own פסח, and those bring their own פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The opening line sets up a list of supporting ברייתות. Then the גמרא quotes the first one, which supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that in a half-and-half case, each group brings its own פסח, at the first פסח. The טמאים also bring it on time, but בטומאה. This matches רב's view from step 3 exactly. The ברייתות for רב כהנא's two versions will come next.
steps.whyThisMatters: A ברייתא is a source from the time of the תנאים. Each of the three positions has one backing it, which shows that this argument already existed back then.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav,

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא כִּתְרֵי לִישָּׁנֵי.
phrases.english: and it was taught in accordance with Rav Kahana, according to both versions.
phrases.notes: This line is a setup for the ברייתות that follow.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav:
If the Jewish people were half pure
and half impure,
these perform [the Pesach] for themselves
phrases.notes: The טהורים bring it בטהרה.

phrases.english: and those perform [it] for themselves.
phrases.notes: The טמאים bring it בטומאה, at the first פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב כהנא, the גמרא brings outside sources, starting with one that supports רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that in a half-and-half case each group brings its own פסח at the first פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶחֱצָה טְהוֹרִין וּמֶחֱצָה טְמֵאִין, הַלָּלוּ עוֹשִׂין לְעַצְמָן וְהַלָּלוּ עוֹשִׂין לְעַצְמָן'

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting the first version of רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when the people are half טהורים and half טמאים, the טהורים bring the first פסח and the טמאים bring פסח שני. This matches the first version of רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא, matching the first version of רב כהנא: If the Jewish people were half pure and half impure, the pure ones bring the first פסח, and the impure ones bring the second פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of supporting ברייתות from step 9. Here it brings a ברייתא that matches the first version of רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב כהנא held that in a half-and-half case the טמאים are pushed off to פסח שני. This ברייתא says exactly that: the טהורים bring the first פסח, and the טמאים bring the second.

keyTerms.meaning: The first version of an אמורא's statement
Half and half: an even split between טהורים and טמאים
The make-up פסח one month later, on 14 אייר

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with the first version of Rav Kahana:
If the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,
phrases.notes: The exact 50/50 case under debate.

phrases.english: the pure ones perform the first [פסח]
and the impure ones perform the second [פסח].
phrases.notes: The key point: the טמאים do get פסח שני, as in רב כהנא's first version.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of supporting ברייתות begun in step 9 (which supported רב).
steps.raayaObject: The first version of רב כהנא: in a half-and-half case, the טמאים bring פסח שני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly rules the טמאים perform the second פסח.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting the later version of רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא rules that in a half-and-half case, the טהורים bring the first פסח and the טמאים bring neither the first nor the second. This matches the later version of רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא, matching the later version of רב כהנא: If the Jewish people were half pure and half impure, the pure ones bring the first פסח, and the impure ones bring neither the first nor the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third supporting ברייתא, this time for the later version of רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the later version, the half-and-half טמאים are left with no פסח at all. They cannot bring the first one, because they are not a majority, so they cannot bring it while טמא. They also cannot bring פסח שני, because only a minority is sent there. This ברייתא states that result word for word.

keyTerms.meaning: The later (second) version of an אמורא's statement

phrases.english: And it was taught in accordance with the later version of Rav Kahana:
If the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,
the pure ones perform the first [פסח],
and the impure ones do not perform

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: neither the first nor the second.
phrases.notes: The טמאים end up with no קרבן פסח at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 10: a supporting ברייתא for the other version of רב כהנא.
steps.raayaObject: The later version of רב כהנא: in a half-and-half case, the טמאים bring no פסח at all.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly says the טמאים perform neither the first nor the second פסח.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. They describe the same half-and-half case but disagree about the טמאים. In step 10 they bring פסח שני. Here they bring nothing.

steps.title: How do the others explain the ברייתא that sends the טמאים to פסח שני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב and the later version of רב כהנא deal with the ברייתא from step 10, which says the half-and-half טמאים bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב and according to the later version of רב כהנא, that which was taught, 'the pure perform the first and the impure the second,' how do they explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא from step 10 seems to contradict רב and the later version of רב כהנא. It asks how they would explain it, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that half-and-half טמאים bring the first פסח while טמא. The later version of רב כהנא holds that they bring nothing. Both disagree with a ברייתא saying they bring פסח שני, so each needs a way to read that ברייתא differently.

phrases.english: According to Rav and according to the later version of Rav Kahana,
that which was taught
'The pure ones perform the first'
'and the impure ones the second,'
phrases.notes: A quote of the ברייתא from step 10.

phrases.english: how do they explain it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַב וּלְלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא הָא דְּתָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 10 to challenge the two positions that disagree with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and the later version of רב כהנא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly sends half-and-half טמאים to פסח שני. That conflicts with רב (they bring the first פסח while טמא) and with the later version (they bring nothing).

steps.title: The women complete the טמא half
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא is talking about a half-and-half count in which some of the טמאים are women. Without the women, the טמאים would not reach half.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where the Jewish people were half pure and half impure, and women complete the number of the impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by narrowing the case of the ברייתא from step 10. It is a special kind of half-and-half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case only looks like 50/50 because the women are counted. Most of the men are טהור, and the טמא side reaches half only by adding טמא women. So this is not the plain half-and-half case that רב and the later version of רב כהנא are talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; as in the case where (it narrows the case)

phrases.english: For example, where the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,
and women complete [the count of] the impure.
phrases.notes: Without the women, the טמא side would be less than half.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶחֱצָה טְהוֹרִין וּמֶחֱצָה טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a special version of half-and-half.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a plain half-and-half split, which would contradict רב and the later version of רב כהנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's half-and-half count reaches 50% only by including טמא women.

steps.title: Women don't count for the first פסח, so the טמאים are really a minority
steps.stepSummary: This ברייתא holds that women's participation in the first פסח is optional. So we leave them out of the count. Then the טמאים are a minority, and a minority is pushed off to פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא holds that women in the first פסח are optional. Remove the women from the impure, and the impure become a minority. And a minority is pushed off to פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by explaining why the women do not count. Once they are removed, the case becomes a simple minority case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If women's obligation in the first פסח is only רשות, they are not counted when deciding majority or minority. Without them, the טמא men are fewer than half. Everyone agrees that a טמא minority goes to פסח שני, so the ברייתא no longer contradicts רב or the later version of רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: They are pushed off (to a later time)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that sends half-and-half טמאים to פסח שני is reinterpreted. The טמא half includes women, and women do not count for the first פסח because for them it is רשות. Without them, the טמאים are a minority, and a minority always goes to פסח שני. This leaves רב and the later version of רב כהנא standing.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean women are exempt from פסח altogether. The point is only that, according to this תנא, their participation in the first פסח is optional (רשות), so they are left out when counting majority and minority.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the majority/minority count for the first פסח includes only people who are obligated. That detail can completely change the ruling on who brings which פסח.

phrases.english: And he holds: women in the first [פסח] are optional.
Remove the women from the impure,
and the impure become a minority,
and a minority is pushed off to the second Pesach.
phrases.notes: Everyone agrees on this rule for a minority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 13 by giving the reason the women are left out of the count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the halachic reason behind the narrowed case: women do not count because their first פסח is רשות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Counting everyone, the טמאים are exactly half.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the women, the טמאים are a minority, so they are pushed off to פסח שני. This fits every opinion.

steps.title: How do רב and the first version of רב כהנא explain the second ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns the question around. The ברייתא from step 11 says the half-and-half טמאים bring neither פסח. How do רב and the first version of רב כהנא fit that ruling into their views?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, and according to the first version of רב כהנא, what do they do with the ברייתא that says: 'The pure bring the first פסח, and the impure bring neither the first nor the second'? How do they explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב and the first version of רב כהנא with the ברייתא from step 11. That ברייתא says the טמאים miss both the first פסח and פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the גמרא challenged רב and the later version of רב כהנא with the first ברייתא. Now it does the mirror image, challenging רב and the first version of רב כהנא with the second ברייתא. Neither of these opinions says the half-and-half טמאים lose out completely, so the ברייתא seems to contradict them both.

keyTerms.meaning: The first version of a statement
That which was taught in a ברייתא
The make-up פסח, brought a month later

phrases.english: According to Rav and according to the first version of Rav Kahana,
that which was taught in a baraita:
"The pure perform the first Pesach
and the impure do not perform

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי״,
phrases.english: neither the first nor the second,"
how do they reconcile it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This mirrors step 12. There the first ברייתא was used against one pair of opinions; here the second ברייתא is used against the other pair.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and the first version of רב כהנא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions give the half-and-half טמאים some פסח, either in טומאה or as פסח שני. The ברייתא says the טמאים get no פסח at all.

steps.title: רב's answer: women push the pure into a majority
steps.stepSummary: רב says the ברייתא is about a case where the men were split half and half, and the women added to the pure side. The ברייתא's תנא holds that women are obligated in the first פסח and optional in פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב explains it this way. The case is where the Jewish men were half impure and half pure, and the women added extra numbers to the pure side. This תנא holds that women are obligated in the first פסח and optional in the second.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the case and the key rule behind his answer. The next step will show how these two pieces lead to the ruling that the טמאים get no פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among the men alone it is exactly half and half. Once the women are added, the pure become a majority. The rule that women are obligated only in the first פסח decides when they are counted: they count for the first פסח but not for פסח שני.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice that in step 14 the women were optional in the first פסח. Here the ברייתא's תנא holds the opposite: women are obligated in the first and optional in the second. Each ברייתא is explained with its own view about women.

phrases.english: Rav reconciles it:
for example, where the Jewish people were
half impure and half pure,
and the women added on to the pure,
and he (the tanna) holds:
women in the first Pesach are obligated,
and in the second it is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of step 15 for רב by narrowing the case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) together with a view about women's obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe a plain half-and-half case, which would contradict רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is half-and-half only among the men. The women change the count differently for each פסח.

steps.title: Why the טמאים miss both the first פסח and פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: For the first פסח, the women are counted, so the טמאים are a minority, and a minority cannot bring the first פסח in טומאה. For פסח שני, the women are removed, so it is half and half, and according to רב half the people do not bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: They don't bring the first פסח, because they are a minority, and a minority does not bring the first פסח. They also don't bring the second, because once you take the women out of the count, it is half and half, and half do not bring the second.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes his answer by applying the women rule to each פסח one at a time. This shows how the טמאים end up with no פסח at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first פסח, women are obligated, so they are counted. That makes the טמאים a minority, and a טמא minority may not bring the first פסח in טומאה. For פסח שני, women are optional, so they are not counted. That leaves the men at half and half, and in רב's view a half-and-half group does not go to פסח שני.
steps.whatToRemember: The same group of people can be a minority for one פסח and exactly half for the other. It depends on whether the women are counted.

phrases.english: On the first Pesach they do not perform it,
because they are a minority,
and a minority does not perform on the first.
And on the second they do not perform it,
because, remove the women from them,
and they become half and half,
and half does not perform on the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This applies the setup of step 16 to reach the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a counting rule differently to each פסח
steps.terutzMaskana: With women counted only for the first פסח, the טמאים are a minority for the first and half for the second, so in רב's view they bring neither.

steps.title: רב כהנא's answer: women bring the pure up to half
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא (first version) holds that half the people do bring פסח שני. He explains the ברייתא as a case where most of the men were טמאים, and the women filled out the pure side to make it half and half. Again, women are obligated in the first פסח and optional in the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא, who said that half the people also bring the second פסח, explains it this way. The case is where the Jewish people were half pure and half impure only because the women completed the pure side. This תנא holds that women are obligated in the first פסח and optional in the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב כהנא's way of fitting the ברייתא. He uses the same women rule as רב, but with different numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among the men, the טמאים are a majority. With the women counted, the two sides are equal. For the first פסח the women count, so it is half and half, and the pure bring the first פסח. For פסח שני the women do not count, so the טמאים are really a majority. Following the standard explanation, a majority is not pushed off to פסח שני, so the טמאים do not bring it either.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and רב כהנא keep their own views about a half-and-half case. They do it by explaining the ברייתא as a case where women are counted for the first פסח but not for פסח שני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method. Instead of rejecting a ברייתא, an אמורא redefines its case, here by who gets counted, so that it fits his own ruling.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Kahana, who said:
half also perform on the second Pesach,
this is how he reconciles it:
for example, where the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,
and the women completed the number of the pure.
And he (the tanna) holds:
women in the first Pesach are obligated,
and in the second it is optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב כָּהֲנָא דַּאֲמַר: פַּלְגָא נָמֵי עָבְדִי בַּשֵּׁנִי, הָכִי מְתָרֵיץ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the same challenge from step 15, but for the first version of רב כהנא. It uses רב's women rule with reversed numbers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) together with a view about women's obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב כהנא holds that half bring פסח שני, the ברייתא's denial of פסח שני seemed to contradict him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the women, the טמאים are really a majority. So for פסח שני they are not a group that gets pushed off, and they do not bring it.

steps.title: Why the half-and-half group brings neither Pesach, according to רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא finishes his explanation. At the first פסח the women are counted, so it is half and half, and the impure half cannot bring it in טומאה. At פסח שני the women are removed, so the טמאים are a majority, and a majority does not bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first פסח they do not bring it, because they are half and half, and a half does not bring the first פסח in impurity. On the second פסח they also do not bring it. Take the women away from the pure side, and the impure become the majority. A majority does not bring פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רב כהנא's explanation of the ברייתא from step 11, showing why the טמאים end up bringing neither פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is that the women count at the first פסח but not at פסח שני. That makes the same group 'half' at the first פסח and 'majority' at the second. Each status blocks a different פסח: a half cannot bring the first פסח in טומאה, and a majority is not sent to פסח שני.
steps.confusionAlert: The same people get two different labels. At the first פסח they are 'half,' because the women are counted. At פסח שני they are 'majority,' because the women are not counted. The count changes, so the status changes.

phrases.english: On the first [Pesach] they do not perform it
because they are half and half,
phrases.notes: The women are counted on the pure side.

phrases.english: and a half does not perform it on the first [in impurity];
on the second they also do not perform it
because if you remove the women from among the pure,
phrases.notes: Women are optional at פסח שני, so they are not counted.

phrases.english: the impure become the majority,
and a majority does not perform it on the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation begun in step 18 for רב כהנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case redefinition (most of the men impure; women balance the count)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ruling that the טמאים bring neither פסח seems to clash with רב כהנא's view that a half does bring פסח שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the women change the count, the טמאים are 'half' at the first פסח and 'majority' at פסח שני. So neither פסח applies to them, with no contradiction to רב כהנא.

steps.title: A ברייתא lets each half bring its own פסח — how does רב כהנא explain it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if Israel was half pure and half impure, each group brings the פסח for itself. Each half seems to act like a majority here, with the impure half bringing it in טומאה. That clashes with רב כהנא, who in both versions holds that an impure half cannot bring the first פסח בטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב כהנא, what about what was taught in a ברייתא? If Israel was half pure and half impure, these bring the פסח for themselves and those bring it for themselves. How does he explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא with a ברייתא that seems to treat each half like a majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ברייתא that step 9 brought in support of רב. Many explain 'these bring for themselves and those for themselves' as both groups bringing the first פסח: the pure in טהרה and the impure separately in טומאה. If so, the impure half is treated like a majority. But in both of רב כהנא's versions, the impure half may NOT bring the first פסח בטומאה: in one version they go to פסח שני, and in the other they bring nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: That which was taught (in a ברייתא)
These perform for themselves (each group brings its own)
How does he explain / resolve it?

steps.confusionAlert: Sefaria's bracketed translation reads the impure half as bringing it 'on the second פסח.' But the question here, and the answer in the next step, only make sense if the impure half brings the first פסח in טומאה. This follows the common explanation of this ברייתא.

phrases.english: And according to רב כהנא,
that which was taught in a ברייתא:
If the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,
these perform it for themselves
and those perform it for themselves,
how does he explain it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After reconciling the other ברייתות, the גמרא turns to the remaining one: the ברייתא from step 9 that supported רב. It asks how רב כהנא deals with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's view, in both versions, that in a half-and-half case the impure half does not bring the first פסח בטומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the impure half bring its own first פסח in טומאה, as if half counts like a majority. Both versions of רב כהנא deny the impure half the first פסח, so the ברייתא contradicts him.

steps.title: רב כהנא: this is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that this is a dispute of תנאים. One תנא holds that half counts like a majority, and another holds it does not. He follows the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא could say to you: it is a dispute of תנאים. There is one who says half-and-half is like a majority, and there is one who says half-and-half is not like a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא does not explain the ברייתא away. He admits it disagrees with him and says other תנאים agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rather than reinterpreting the ברייתא, רב כהנא accepts that it reflects one side of a debate among the תנאים. That ברייתא holds half-and-half counts as a majority. רב כהנא sides with the תנאים who say it does not, so he is not bound by this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute of תנאים

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next section. The גמרא will now study that very ברייתא to see the rule about half-and-half and majority.

phrases.english: רב כהנא could say to you:
It is a dispute of תנאים.
There is one who says:
half and half is like a majority,
and there is one who says:
half and half is not like a majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַב כָּהֲנָא: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute of תנאים (the challenging source follows a different opinion)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to refute רב כהנא outright.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects the view that half counts as a majority. רב כהנא follows the תנאים who hold it does not.

steps.title: Studying the ברייתא itself: each half brings its own
steps.stepSummary: With 'גופא', the גמרא goes back to quote the ברייתא again in full so it can study it. When it is half and half, each group brings its own פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: if Israel was half pure and half impure, these perform it for themselves and those perform it for themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a fresh look at the ברייתא it just quoted, starting with its first line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גופא' signals a new section. We are no longer defending רב or רב כהנא; we are now reading the ברייתא on its own terms. The first ruling is that an even split lets each side bring its own offering. The next line will add what happens when one side is bigger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself' — returning to study a source quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
If the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,
these perform it for themselves
and those perform it for themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the ברייתא from step 20 in order to analyze it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an exact half-and-half split, each group brings its own פסח.

steps.title: If the impure are more by even one, everyone brings it in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the טמאים outnumber the טהורים by even one person, everyone brings the פסח in טומאה. The reason is that a communal offering cannot be split into two groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the impure were more than the pure, even by one, they all bring it in impurity, because a communal offering is not divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its second rule: once the טמאים are a majority, the whole nation brings the פסח together in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the split is exactly even, each side may act separately. But once there is a majority, the פסח is treated as one קרבן ציבור, and that cannot be split. So even the טהורים join in bringing it in טומאה. The קרבן פסח stays a communal offering; what is unusual here is only how it is brought.
steps.whatToRemember: An exact half-and-half split means each side brings its own. A majority of טמאים, even by one, means everyone brings it together in טומאה, because a קרבן ציבור is not split.

phrases.english: If the impure outnumbered the pure,
even by one —
they should perform it in impurity,
phrases.notes: Even the pure people join in.

phrases.english: because a communal offering is not divided.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ טְמֵאִין עוֹדְפִין עַל הַטְּהוֹרִין, אֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from the even split to the majority case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the טמאים are a majority by even one, the whole nation brings the פסח in טומאה, because a קרבן ציבור is not divided.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא: one person cannot tip the community into impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא disagrees. A single extra person cannot be the one who pushes the whole community into bringing the פסח in טומאה. He begins to bring a verse as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא says: an individual does not tip the community over to impurity, as it is said:
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with the ruling of 'even one,' and the גמרא is setting up the verse he will quote on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said a majority of even one is enough to make everyone bring the פסח in טומאה. רבי אלעזר בן מתיא says that is not enough: one single extra person cannot decide this for the whole community. The verse he relies on comes right after 'שנאמר.'

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first view
The individual (here: the one extra person)
As it is said (a verse follows)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence ends at 'שנאמר' because the verse continues on the next amud. Nothing is missing here.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא says:
The individual does not tip the balance of
the community toward impurity,
as it is said:
phrases.notes: The verse is quoted on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן מַתְיָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין הַיָּחִיד מַכְרִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling in step 23 that a majority of even one decides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One extra person is not enough to make the whole community bring the פסח in טומאה. His source is a verse quoted next.
